The carry $c_i$ into digit $i$ in the binary addition of $j$ to $\omega$ is defined by $c_0 = 0$ and $c_{i+1} = \lfloor (\omega_i + j_i + c_i)/2 \rfloor$.

The dyadic integer $\omega + j$ has $i$-th digit $(\omega_i + j_i + c_i) \bmod 2$, where the carries are given by $c_0 = 0$ and $c_{i+1} = \lfloor (\omega_i + j_i + c_i)/2 \rfloor$.

The $q$-weighted binary digit sum of $k$ is $s_q(k) = \sum_{i \ge 0} \omega_i q^{i+1}$, a finite sum because only finitely many $\omega_i$ are nonzero.

nodes.summary: For a real or complex parameter $a$ and a real number $x$, let $\tau(y)$ denote the distance from a real number $y$ to the nearest integer. The Takagi–Landsberg function is $\mathcal{T}_a(x) = \sum_{n \ge 0} a^n \tau(2^n x)$, where the value is taken to be $0$ when the series does not converge absolutely. The series converges for $|a| < 1$, and at dyadic rationals $x$ it is a finite sum.
